meta.name: The Heights at Uptown — Phase 1
caveats: Monotony adjacency is built from the OCH master address list, not from geometry: lots are ordered along each street by house number, and across-street pairing is same street, opposite side, nearest number. This spans block boundaries correctly (Garrett Parkway runs through blocks U, M and K). 23 of 48 OCH lots have an OCH lot opposite; the rest face non-OCH lots, which never carry an OCH plan and so cannot conflict. An earlier geometry-only derivation disagreed with the addresses on 15 of 23 cases and was discarded.

Driveway slope is MEASURED, not estimated, for all 48 OCH lots: see data/heights-uptown-grade.json. Slab = pad + 0.833 ft; garage apron = top of slab - 0.84 ft; run = graded pad rear edge to rear lot line, taken from the engineer's grading drawing; alley elevation at the driveway is interpolated between the surveyed alley points. 25 of 48 OCH lots exceed Celina's preferred 10%, and 14 exceed the 12% a variance will reach and so need a dropped garage: K-20, K-21, L-17, M-22, M-23, P-1, P-12, P-13, P-17, P-22, P-24, U-8, U-9, X-1. An earlier estimate in this file -- (pad - rear grade) / 20 ft apron -- named only six lots (P-8, P-12, N-5, U-9, X-1, Y-2) and was wrong in both directions: P-8 measures 3.8% and Y-2 3.3%, both clean, while P-22 measures 13.9% and was not on the list. The 20 ft apron was the error: actual runs are 20 to 46 ft. Purchasing's independent grade workbook agrees with the measured figures.
Retaining wall data covers 27 of 48 OCH lots. Absence of wall data is not evidence there is no wall.
Setbacks (10′ front BL, 5′ porch encroachment) were resolved against OCH-built, City-approved plot plans, which govern over the spec sheet’s 20′.

This dataset holds 227 lots. The recorded plat has 236 residential lots; six more (3,850 sf each, running parallel to Block S) are absent, and the plat itself is internally inconsistent — its lot count table totals 244 while its title block totals 249. None of the absent lots are OCH lots, and only OCH lots ever carry an OCH plan, so no fit, grading, wall or monotony check is affected. Left as-is by decision 9/17/26.

P-8 (501 Callum Parkway) has a 35 x 66 ft pad, the only OCH pad shallower than 80 ft -- confirmed against the engineer's grading drawing. The shallowest plans are Knox A and Knox B at 74.5 ft, and NEITHER CARRIES A PORCH, so there is no encroachment credit to apply and 74.5 ft is the real requirement against a 66 ft pad. No current plan fits P-8 on depth. (An earlier note here said 69.5 ft 'after the 5 ft porch credit'; the credit is per elevation and is 0 ft on both Knox elevations, so that figure was wrong -- the conclusion was right for the wrong reason.) The same note flagged P-8 at ~15% driveway slope. That was the 20 ft apron estimate. P-8 measures 3.8% -- clean, well inside the City's preferred 10%.

The per-lot fields sl21 and drop are RETIRED and set to null. sl21 was (fp - dg) / 20 and disagreed with the measured driveway slope on 30 of the 30 lots that carried it, by 1.0 to 26.7 percentage points (worst: Y-2, which read 30.0%% against a measured 3.3%%, and carried a drop of -6.0 ft, i.e. a negative drop). The cause is dg: it is not the alley elevation at the driveway. At 708 Garrett, dg is 697.5 while the surveyed alley there is 694.60. The pad elevation fp is unaffected and is correct -- it matches the engineer's 236 FP labels 48 of 48. Driveway slope now comes only from data/heights-uptown-grade.json. Nulled rather than deleted so the change is reversible from version history.
meta.addressSource: OCH master address list (block/lot → address), 48/48 OCH lots
meta.streetSource: Street names and positions from the recorded plat DWG (20241219-Heights_at_Uptown_Phase_1_FP.dwg) via LibreDWG, transformed by x-2493533.1 / y-7171672.4 (exact, zero residual). COLTON MEWS is the one exception: it is not a text entity in the DWG, so its label was placed from lot Y-2 and is approximate.
meta.orientation: North is UP. The plat DWG uses survey coordinates (y increases north) while SVG draws y downward, so the extracted geometry was vertically mirrored. Flipped 9/17/26 about y=1437.0. Grand Oaks was already correct and was not touched.
meta.padSource: Building pads from the engineer's grading drawing (Grading - Heights at Uptown Phase 1 - 12/19/24, layers C-BLDG-35x80 (45) and C-BLDG-25x80 (35)), read via LibreDWG. Same coordinate system as the plat, so the same transform applies. These are ACTUAL pad locations, not derived from setbacks. All 48 OCH lots have exactly one pad, every one 35.0 ft wide — independently confirming the 35 ft buildable width derived from the setbacks.
meta.geometrySource: Lot boundaries re-extracted from the recorded plat DWG (20241219 Heights at Uptown Phase 1 FP) on 2026-10-29, INCLUDING the polyline bulges that encode arcs. The earlier extraction kept the vertices and dropped the bulges, so every platted arc was stored as its chord — on P-1 that cut 1,604 sq ft (22%) off the lot. Lots were matched to plat polygons by the plat's own BLOCK/LOT label falling inside the polygon. Arcs are tessellated at about 2 ft per chord.
meta.areaSource: aPlat is the plat's surveyed SQ. FT. label read from the DWG. It is authoritative over any area computed from pts.
